Senses.Explanation: Literally, bind or establish, and regulation or restriction. In Chan records the term labels the formal beginning of a bounded communal period and also functions as a verb for beginning it. It occurs 2,026 times in 255 allowlisted texts. Records repeatedly mark a discourse or small talk as delivered at this beginning, contrast it with release from the restriction, and identify the date: one record calls the fifteenth day of the tenth month the restriction and the fifteenth day of the first month its release; another describes the interval from the former date to the Lantern Festival. A tea talk parses the two graphs as joining companions of one purpose and holding a wild mind in check. Individual answers remain concrete: asked what the restriction is, one master says, 'Return to your place.'
Senses.Note: The term overlaps with beginning the summer session, but the corpus also attests a winter restriction, so 'summer session' is too narrow as the head gloss. Release from the restriction is the consistent opposite. The corpus has 136 instances of the compact heading 'restriction-period discourse' and 20 of 'restriction-period small talk.'
